chunks: And from him, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:
I asked him about a mouse that falls into the well, or a bird. He said: If you reach it before it becomes putrid, you draw seven buckets from it.

So the proper way regarding these two reports is that we interpret them to mean that if the mouse had decomposed, then seven buckets are to be drawn from it; and we interpret the first two reports to mean that it was removed before it decomposed. And that which indicates this detailed distinction is what follows.

key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well whose water is affected by the falling animal
key_terms.الْخَبَرَيْنِ: the two reports being interpreted together
key_terms.الْفَأْرَةِ: a mouse falling into the well, central to the legal case discussed
key_terms.تَفَسَّخَتْ: decomposed or disintegrated, used to distinguish between reports
key_terms.سَبْعَ دِلَاءٍ: seven buckets, the specified amount of water to be drawn
key_terms.نَزَحْتَ: you draw out water from the well
key_terms.يُنْتِنَ: to become putrid or foul-smelling, a condition affecting the ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a mouse or bird falls into a well in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This passage discusses a legal ruling concerning ritual purity when a mouse or bird falls into a well. It also shows a juristic method of reconciling apparently different hadith reports by distinguishing between cases where the animal has decomposed and where it has not.
